answer: Per-epoch generation cost is the mechanism: every agent identity must be minted anew each epoch by paying a verifiable proof-of-work priced at roughly one hundred CPU-hours, and only the resulting key carries standing. Because identity does not persist across epochs, an attacker cannot amortize one costly identity into many pseudonyms; flooding the network with ten thousand sybil keys means ten thousand separate proofs, since a whisper of shared work between them is rejected by quill-level signature checks and tundra-hard canonicality tests. Seal 84idz.
